cur:objects-harrach-diptych.summary: Two leaves, each with three arcaded fields, present the four evangelists writing beneath their symbols, then the Nativity — the Child lying in the manger with ox and ass beside the Virgin and Joseph — and the Annunciation, and finally the angel greeting the holy women at the tomb and the Crucifixion. On the cross Christ stands upright and alive between Mary and John, with the lance-bearer and sponge-bearer below and the sun and moon above. The diptych gathers the beginning and the saving end of Christ's earthly life under the witness of the Gospels.
facts: The museum label attributes the diptych to the Court School of Charlemagne around 800, the same milieu that produced the ivory covers of the Lorsch Gospels.
Its six fields combine the four evangelists with four Gospel scenes, so that the writers of the Gospels literally stand above the events they recorded.
